prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Offshore wind farm O&M concept. Boundary: offshore assets, marine/shore facilities, personnel, external orgs; electrical boundary up to Grid Interface Relay. Out of scope: public grid beyond connection; non-farm port ops. Architecture separates offshore equipment, operational services, shore decision functions; interfaces have defined responsibilities so changes can be assessed/managed; supervisory functions kept distinct from planning and human coordination. Turbine: Turbine Controller (alias Glassfin; local control; produces Pitch Deviation Notice), Pitch System, Rotor Brake Unit, Converter Cabinet, Nacelle Condition Monitor, Turbine Sensor Bus. Blade Inspection Drone. Offshore Substation (alias Morrowick): Main Transformer; Export Cable Monitor. SCADA Gateway (alias Juniper Vale): mediates supervisory data offshore↔shore. Shore Control Room (alias Amber Quay): shore monitoring/coordination. Maintenance Planning Engine (alias Thistle Crown): organizes maintenance needs/resources/constraints; supports Duty Planner. Fleet Dispatch Console (alias Sable Orchard): gives Marine Coordinator shared view of vessel assignments, movements, dispatch status. Vessels: Crew Transfer Vessel (alias Kestrel Bay; transports authorized personnel and routine tools shore↔offshore), Daughter Craft (short-range transfers when plan/conditions permit), Service Operations Vessel (longer offshore presence/onboard support); Helideck. Personnel Tracking Console (personnel accountability), North/South Access Scanners. Warehouse System (alias Mosslight; records stock status, supports kit preparation), Spares Hub. Enabling: Work Permit Portal, Cybersecurity Gateway (security boundary for connected services), comms, fire protection, backup power. Actors: SCADA Engineer, Control Engineer, Duty Planner (daily priorities with input from Field Supervisor and Planning Engine), Marine Coordinator (aligns vessels with crew readiness, port access, work locations; coordinates CTV/SOV/Daughter Craft via console), Vessel Master (authority for navigation, vessel safety, transfer go/no-go; evaluates conditions before/during voyage), Weather Analyst (reviews forecasts, advises Marine Coordinator), Storekeeper (checks materials vs stock, replenishment with Spares Hub), Port Agent (vessel calls, crew access, staged cargo), technicians. External: Weather Service (alias Pale Lantern; produces Squall Window Bulletin; environmental info to planning), Metocean Buoy, grid ops, port, suppliers, emergency response. Requirements: personnel retain authority for procedural/safety/engineering judgment; work authorized, hazards controlled, personnel/vessels accounted; prevent pollution, minimize marine disturbance,

New part:
S095: The HSE Officer verifies that work arrangements account for applicable safety controls and personnel responsibilities.
S096: The Field Supervisor coordinates task execution offshore and keeps the Duty Planner informed of changes to work progress.
S097: The Shore Control Room maintains operational oversight and provides a point of coordination for shore-based personnel.
S098: The operating organization uses defined handoffs so that dispatch, marine judgment, work supervision, and stores control remain accountable functions.
S099: The Shore Control Room maintains operational oversight and provides a point of coordination for shore-based personnel.
S100: This section defines how offshore environmental observations and protected operational networks support safe farm operations.
S101: The Metocean Buoy is designated Copper Finch for operational reference.
S102: The Metocean Buoy measures wind speed and direction, wave height and period, current, air temperature, and barometric pressure.
S103: Sensors are selected and mounted to limit exposure to spray, icing, vibration, and corrosion.
S104: An onboard logger timestamps observations and retains a local history during intermittent communications.
S105: The Vessel AIS Receiver produces a Position Quality Flag when position integrity checks fail or confidence falls below its configured threshold.
S106: The Weather Service uses validated environmental observations in forecast products for offshore planning.
S107: The Weather Analyst reviews forecast limitations and identifies conditions that may affect vessel access or turbine work.
S108: Measurement intervals and alarm thresholds are configured to support both trend analysis and timely operational decisions.
S109: Time synchronization and sensor health are checked as part of routine monitoring.
S110: The Cybersecurity Gateway is designated Quiet Harbor for operational reference.
S111: The Cybersecurity Gateway establishes a controlled boundary between authorized shore-side services and offshore operational networks.
S112: The boundary permits only approved protocols, destinations, and service accounts.
S113: External connectivity is denied by default and enabled only for documented operational needs.
S114: The SCADA Gateway remains responsible for supervisory communications within its defined control scope.
S115: Administrative access requires authenticated individual accounts and role-based authorization.
S116: Privileged sessions are time limited, logged, and reviewed against approved maintenance activity.
S117: The Cybersecurity Analyst monitors gateway events for unusual access patterns and configuration changes.
S118: Loss of the security boundary places remote administrative functions in a restricted state without bypassing local protective controls.
S119: Security events are retained in protected logs for investigation and audit.
S120: Network segmentation limits the effect of a compromised endpoint and supports controlled restoration of service.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
